title: Animal Kingdom
seo_title: Animal Kingdom Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 4)
standard_text: Salient features and classification of animals, non-chordates up to phyla level and chordates up to class level (salient features and at least two examples of each category).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 4 Animal Kingdom: levels of organisation, symmetry, coelom, the non-chordate phyla and the classes of vertebrates with examples. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Animals are grouped by organisation, symmetry, germ layers and coelom.
key_sub: Chordates have a notochord, a dorsal nerve cord and gill slits.
body_html:
How to think about it

Animals are classified by level of organisation (cellular, tissue, organ), symmetry (radial or bilateral), germ layers (diploblastic or triploblastic), body cavity (acoelomate, pseudocoelomate, coelomate) and segmentation. Non-chordate phyla run from Porifera to Hemichordata; Arthropoda is the largest.

Chordates have a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and pharyngeal gill slits. Vertebrate classes include cartilaginous and bony fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.

Example

Earthworm phylum?

segmented

Answer: Annelida

Example

Shark class?

cartilage skeleton

Answer: Chondrichthyes

Common mistakes

  • Calling a starfish a fish.
  • Calling Ascaris an annelid.
  • Saying all reptiles have three-chambered hearts (crocodiles have four).

faq.q: What is the largest animal phylum?
faq.a: Arthropoda, with about two-thirds of all named species.

faq.q: What are the three basic features of chordates?
faq.a: A notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and paired pharyngeal gill slits.
